Looking at this problem, I need to find the radius of convergence of the series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n z^{(n)}}{n!}$ where $z^{(n)} = z(z+1)(z+2)\cdots(z+n-1)$ is the rising Pochhammer symbol.

## Setting Up the Ratio Test

This series is related to the binomial-type power series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(z)_n}{n!}x^n = (1-x)^{-z}$, with $x = -1$. To find the radius of convergence, I apply the ratio test to the coefficients.

Let $a_n = \frac{(-1)^n z^{(n)}}{n!}$. Then:

$$\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = \frac{(-1)^{n+1} z^{(n+1)}}{(n+1)!}\cdot\frac{n!}{(-1)^n z^{(n)}} = -\frac{z^{(n+1)}}{(n+1)z^{(n)}}$$

Since $z^{(n+1)} = z^{(n)}(z+n)$:

$$\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = -\frac{z+n}{n+1}$$

## Computing the Limit

Taking the limit of the absolute value:

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right| = \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{|z+n|}{n+1} = \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{n\left|1+\frac{z}{n}\right|}{n+1} = 1$$

## Verifying with the General Term Asymptotics

Using $\frac{z^{(n)}}{n!} = \frac{\Gamma(n+z)}{\Gamma(z)\,\Gamma(n+1)}$, Stirling's approximation gives:

$$\frac{\Gamma(n+z)}{\Gamma(n+1)} \sim n^{z-1} \quad \text{as } n\to\infty$$

So $|a_n| \sim \frac{n^{\text{Re}(z)-1}}{|\Gamma(z)|}$, confirming the terms behave like a $p$-series with $p = 1 - \text{Re}(z)$, consistent with the ratio limit being 1.

## Conclusion

The radius of convergence of the underlying power series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(z)_n}{n!}x^n$ (of which our series is the special case $x=-1$) is determined by:

$$R = \frac{1}{\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{z^{(n+1)}/(n+1)!}{z^{(n)}/n!}\right|} = \frac{1}{\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{|z+n|}{n+1}} = \frac{1}{1} = 1$$

The series converges at $x = -1$ (i.e., our series) when $\text{Re}(z) < 0$ (absolute convergence), consistent with the boundary behavior of a radius-1 disk.

$$\boxed{1}$$
